Established in 1935, Kissan was acquired by UB Group in 1950 and later by Brooke Bond in 1993 before becoming part of HUL in 1994. The brand is recognized as "India’s No. 1 Jams and Preserves brand" and "India’s No. 1 Ketchup brand" according to Euromonitor International Limited. Kissan's strategy focuses on glocalization, adapting its products to meet local tastes while maintaining global convenience. This includes creating chutneys with a coarse texture akin to traditional Indian preparations and introducing region-specific flavors. The brand also emphasizes family-oriented marketing, promoting its products as essential for daily meals and school tiffins. Kissan's pricing model is competitive, aiming to provide value-added processed food items to a broad consumer base.. Squashes offer a wider range of flavors such as mixed fruit, mango, orange, pineapple, lemon, and grape. The products are available in various SKUs like pouches, bottles, and squeezes, with packaging designed for visibility and ease of use. Kissan sources ingredients from farms across India, emphasizing sustainable sourcing and support for small farmers. The brand also extends to international markets, offering products like authentic Indian spices, pure ghee, exotic oils, gourmet cooking sauces, and exotic fruit jams..
